question: A person travels from city A to city B. If he travels at a speed of 50 km/h, he arrives 1 hour early. If he travels at a speed of 30 km/h, he arrives 1 hour late. What is the distance (in km) between city A and city B?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| ] × Δt

Here, S₁ = 50 km/h, S₂ = 30 km/h.

Time difference Δt = 1 hour early + 1 hour late = 2 hours.

⇒ Distance = [ (50 × 30) / (50 − 30) ] × 2

⇒ Distance = [ 1500 / 20 ] × 2 = 150 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 150 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
• 
 
 
 City A
 City B
 
 Distance = d km
 
 

 50 km/h → Arrives 1 hr early
 
 

 30 km/h → Arrives 1 hr late

**Given:**

Speed 1 (S₁) = 50 km/h, Time 1 (t₁) = t − 1 hours

Speed 2 (S₂) = 30 km/h, Time 2 (t₂) = t + 1 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

Let the usual time taken to cover distance d be t hours.

⇒ d = 50 × (t − 1) --- (Equation 1)

⇒ d = 30 × (t + 1) --- (Equation 2)

Equating both the distances since the actual distance is constant:

⇒ 50 × (t − 1) = 30 × (t + 1)

⇒ 5t − 5 = 3t + 3

⇒ 2t = 8

⇒ t = 4 hours

Substituting the value of t in Equation 1:

⇒ d = 50 × (4 − 1)

⇒ d = 50 × 3 = 150 km

**∴ The correct answer is 150 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed

When a person travels equal distances at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the entire journey is given by (2 × S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂).

Relative Speed

If two bodies are moving in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|. If they are moving in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Time Difference Formula

When travelling the same distance with varying speeds resulting in early or late arrivals, the direct distance is always (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| × Total Time Difference.
